65333.subject: Music
65333.question_text:
Define the following musical elements and explain their roles in a composition:
(i) Dynamics
(ii) Tempo
(iii) Timbre
65333.explanation:
(i) Dynamics refer to the volume of sound in music, indicated by symbols like p (piano) for soft and f (forte) for loud. They add expressiveness and emotional depth to a composition.
(ii) Tempo is the speed of a piece, measured in beats per minute (BPM). It sets the mood and energy, with terms like Allegro (fast) or Adagio (slow).
(iii) Timbre is the unique quality of a sound that distinguishes different instruments or voices, even when playing the same pitch and dynamics. It enriches texture and color in music.

65334.subject: Music
65334.question_text:
Write the following notes in the treble clef:
(i) Middle C
(ii) E above middle C
(iii) G below middle C
Label each note with its letter name and octave designation (e.g., C4).
65334.explanation:
(i) Middle C is written on the first ledger line below the treble clef staff and is labeled C4.
(ii) E above middle C is the first line of the treble clef staff and is labeled E4.
(iii) G below middle C is written on the second space below the treble clef staff and is labeled G3.

65335.subject: Music
65335.question_text: Which of the following scales contains the pattern of whole and half steps: Whole, Whole, Half, Whole, Whole, Whole, Half?
65335.explanation: The pattern Whole, Whole, Half, Whole, Whole, Whole, Half corresponds to the major scale. This is the foundational scale in Western music, characterized by its bright and happy sound.

65336.subject: Music
65336.question_text:
(i) Define interval inversion.
(ii) Invert the following intervals and state their new names:
(a) Perfect 5th (C to G)
(b) Major 3rd (E to G#)
65336.explanation:
(i) Interval inversion occurs when the lower note of an interval is moved up an octave, or the higher note is moved down an octave, resulting in a new interval that complements the original.
(ii) (a) A Perfect 5th (C to G) inverts to a Perfect 4th (G to C).
(b) A Major 3rd (E to G#) inverts to a Minor 6th (G# to E).

65337.subject: Music
65337.question_text:
Write the following triads in root position, first inversion, and second inversion:
(i) C major triad
(ii) A minor triad
Label each inversion clearly.
65337.explanation:
(i) C major triad:
Root position: C-E-G
First inversion: E-G-C
Second inversion: G-C-E
(ii) A minor triad:
Root position: A-C-E
First inversion: C-E-A
Second inversion: E-A-C

65338.subject: Music
65338.question_text: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of traditional African music?
65338.explanation: Call-and-response is a hallmark of African music, where a leader sings or plays a phrase, and a group responds. This interactive style is central to communal participation in African musical traditions.

65339.subject: Music
65339.question_text: Describe the role of the fontomfrom ensemble in Akan traditional music. Include its instrumentation and cultural significance.
65339.explanation:
The fontomfrom is a royal Akan drum ensemble used for ceremonies and festivals. It consists of:
(i) From (lead drum), which improvises and leads the ensemble.
(ii) Atumpan (talking drums), which mimic speech patterns.
(iii) Eguankoba (supporting drums) and Dawuro (iron bell).
Culturally, it symbolizes authority, communicates messages, and accompanies dances like the Adowa.

65340.subject: Music
65340.question_text: Which period of Western art music is characterized by polyphonic texture, ornamentation, and the use of harpsichord?
65340.explanation: The Baroque period (1600–1750) is known for polyphonic textures (e.g., fugues), elaborate ornamentation, and the prominence of the harpsichord. Composers like Bach and Handel defined this era.

65341.subject: Music
65341.question_text:
Compose an 8-bar melody in the key of G major for the soprano voice. Include:
(i) A clear phrase structure (antecedent/consequent).
(ii) Use of stepwise motion and leaps.
(iii) A cadence at the end.
65341.explanation:
A sample melody in G major:
Bars 1–4 (Antecedent): G-A-B-C | D-E-F#-G | A-B-C-D | E-D-C-B
Bars 5–8 (Consequent): G-F#-E-D | C-B-A-G | F#-G-A-B | G (Perfect cadence).
Features:
(i) Balanced 4+4 phrase structure.
(ii) Mix of stepwise motion (e.g., G-A-B) and leaps (e.g., D-G).
(iii) Ends with a V-I cadence (D-G).

65342.subject: Music
65342.question_text: Which software is primarily used for digital audio workstation (DAW) tasks such as recording, editing, and mixing music?
65342.explanation: Pro Tools is an industry-standard DAW used for professional recording, editing, and mixing. Other examples include Logic Pro and Ableton Live, but Pro Tools is the most widely recognized.
